title: Go: Zero Values
description: Write a Go program that demonstrates the zero value initialization for different types.

codeTemplate.go:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	var i int
	var f float64
	var s string
	var b bool
	var p *int

	fmt.Printf("int: %d\n", i)
	fmt.Printf("float64: %.1f\n", f)
	fmt.Printf("string: %q\n", s)
	fmt.Printf("bool: %t\n", b)
	fmt.Printf("pointer: %v\n", p)
}

verificationTest: output.includes('int: 0') && output.includes('float64: 0.0') && output.includes('string: ""') && output.includes('bool: false') && output.includes('pointer: <nil>')
hints: Go initializes all variables to their zero value if no explicit initializer is given
Zero values: int=0, float64=0.0, string="", bool=false, pointer=nil
Use `%q` to print strings with quotes, `%v` for default formatting
